title: Jakarta’s policy regulating TPT imports balances supply, demand: Govt
content:
Indonesia’s policy regulating imports of textiles and textile products is aimed at balancing supply and demand while protecting domestic production, the Industry Ministry said. 
The policy is not intended to hinder business, but to align imported goods with domestic market needs, it noted. 
Purchasing domestic products has a greater economic impact as the value-added stays within the country, it added.

title: South India cotton yarn prices rise as natural fibre costs climb
content:
Cotton yarn prices in Mumbai and Tiruppur rose by ₹5-8 per kg across most counts as higher domestic and international cotton pushed up costs. 
Demand from weaving and knitting units stayed average, with weak fabric demand, higher yarn prices and payment constraints weighing on sentiment. 
Gujarat Shankar-6 cotton reached ₹70,500-71,000 per candy amid higher ICE cotton and crop concerns.

title: India yarn exports rise 14%; why is apparel falling 12%?
content:
India’s yarn exports rose 14.0 per cent to $1.340 billion in April–June 2026, while apparel exports fell 12.27 per cent to $3.687 billion.
China led the demand shift, with yarn exports up 311.6 per cent in the quarter and cotton-yarn volumes up 121.1 per cent in FY2025–26.
AEPC seeks cotton-yarn export restraint after prices rose about 60 per cent, but stocks are sizeable on paper.

title: India’s factory growth loses momentum as demand softens in August 2026
content:
India’s manufacturing PMI fell to 52.8 in August from 53.5 in July, marking the weakest sector improvement in five years.
Output and new orders still expanded, but growth slowed as demand softened; export order gains also eased from July.
Manufacturers cut hiring fractionally and raised selling prices more modestly as cost pressures faded.

title: TEXPROCIL takes India’s textile industry into the AI era
content:
India’s TEXPROCIL has launched Phase 2 of its AI-powered Textile Trust Stack with RePut.ai and Control Union under TEX-RAMPS.
The platform combines AI verification, blockchain-enabled data integrity and Digital Product Passports, mapping 42 product/SKU data points.
Phase 2 targets 300 organisations and 3,000+ verified DPPs within six months as EU textile DPP rules move towards a 2027 delegated.

title: China 1.4D lyocell price rises 0.87%, putting Q4 procurement on watch
content:
Chinese domestic 1.4D lyocell rose to CNY 13,920 per tonne on Thursday, closing 0.87 per cent higher for the week.
India stayed unchanged at ₹203 per kg, while Pakistan held at PKR 721 per kg amid neutral currency movements.
Firmer Chinese demand ahead of autumn buying, tighter spot availability and strong H1 demand supported the move.

title: Apparel’s tariff map just changed; who gains the advantage?
content:
US apparel imports fell 7.8 per cent to $36.90 billion in H1 2026, while Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam gained and China and India retreated sharply.
New Section 301 duties put Vietnam and China in a 12.5 per cent group, above the 10 per cent rate for Cambodia, India, Indonesia and others.
Qualifying CAFTA-DR and USMCA goods are exempt; August and September data will offer a cleaner test.

title: Global garment trade nears $550 bn as synthetic fibres gain share
content:
Global knit and woven garment exports neared $550 billion in 2025, making up nearly 60 per cent of world textile exports.
China remained dominant, while Bangladesh rose to second and Vietnam to third among textile exporters.
Synthetic fibres are taking a larger share of garment growth, putting cotton quality and competitiveness higher on sourcing agendas.
